plan: This auction functions like a Vickrey (second-price) auction since the sealed bid serves as an exit price, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such mechanisms, bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy — it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $27.

Since this auction functions like a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid/exit price), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly $31 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing value from underbidding.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction structure (the ascending clock mechanism with sealed bids as exit points means I pay the second-highest bid if I win), the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. This is a dominant strategy in this format.
